chunks: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Muqri reported to me from Abd al-Karim ibn Muhammad al-Bajali, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ali, who reported from Zayd ibn al-Mu'addal, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ajlah, from Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, laid his head on the lap of Umm al-Fadl during his illness in which he passed away, and he fainted. A tear from her tears fell upon his cheek, so he opened his eyes and said to her: "What is the matter with you, O Umm al-Fadl?"

She said: "You have announced to us your own death, and you have informed us that you are dying. If the matter will remain in our favor, then give us glad tidings; and if it will be in others' hands, then counsel us."
He said: So the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said to her: "You will be subdued and weakened after me."

key_terms.أم الفضل: Umm al-Fadl (wife of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, aunt of the Prophet)
key_terms.فأوص بنا: then counsel us / then give us your final directive
key_terms.نَعَيْتَ: you announced (death) / you gave a death notice

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad tell Umm al-Fadl about the fate of Ahl al-Bayt during his final illness?
ai.summary: During his final illness, the Prophet (SAWW) laid his head on Umm al-Fadl's lap and fainted. When her tears fell on his cheek, he awoke and she asked about their fate after him. He prophesied that the Ahl al-Bayt would be oppressed and weakened after his death. This exchange took place in the last days of the Prophet's life and reflects his deep concern for the future of his family.
